name: Invent and Simplify
definition: Leaders expect invention from their teams and always find ways to simplify. They look for new ideas from everywhere and are not limited by "not invented here." When they do new things, they accept that they may be misunderstood for a long time.

rows.situation: Living with complexity vs changing what works
rows.under: Lets complexity live. Lets past output drive future thinking.
rows.justRight: Creates room to find new ways of thinking, with the customer outcome always in mind.
rows.over: Changes things that are working well. Discards a sound decision so they can propose something brand new.

rows.situation: Deciding whether the current approach will scale
rows.under: Accepts the status quo because growth is easy right now. Does not understand the underlying numbers.
rows.justRight: Pushes a thought process that asks whether the idea still works at the next order of scale.
rows.over: Makes the change too fast, in the interest of change itself.

rows.under: The product works and is too complex. Bugs take a long time to fix. Every new engineer wants to rewrite it.
rows.justRight: The result meets the goal. It is simple enough to maintain.
rows.over: Sacrifices the goal or the needed features for elegance.

rows.under: Teams are too interdependent. New work is blocked too often.
rows.justRight: Teams are relatively independent and fast. They know their roles. They still share what they learn.
rows.over: Teams are siloed. Lots of "not invented here" and duplicated work.

rows.under: Ships a complex solution with a high operational burden.
rows.justRight: Delivers features that solve the customer problem and stay maintainable and reliable.
rows.over: Simplifies so far that the customer problem is no longer solved.

rows.under: Re-implements the same solution without moving forward.
rows.justRight: Builds when the customer problem is new. Reuses or buys when a good solution already exists.
rows.over: Builds new technology where there is no need.

rows.situation: A process has become a maze
rows.under: Crosses out one box, claims genius, and leaves the maze in place.
rows.justRight: Reduces the maze to a small, correct path. People in the room say it cannot be that easy. It is.
rows.over: Reduces it to two steps on their laptop, then tells someone else to implement it without talking to the people in the process or plotting where it can go wrong.

rows.under: Adds layers of policy and hierarchy. Argues why you cannot change.
rows.justRight: Finds ways to cut waste and bureaucracy. Endorses good ideas from inside and outside. Balances both sources.
rows.over: Rejects anything that is not new. Tries any new thing even when the data says no.

rows.justRight: Builds new things that have a purpose and improve the customer experience.
rows.over: Innovates for innovation's sake. Not solving a problem.
